items.question: What is pattern matching in C#, and where does it appear?
items.answer: Pattern matching tests an expression for shape, type, or value and can introduce a variable when the test succeeds. The two expression forms are is and the switch expression. Switch statements also accept patterns. The vocabulary includes declaration and type, constant, relational, property, positional, list, var, discard, and the logical and, or, and not combinators. The compiler checks exhaustiveness on switch expressions and flags when an arm is already covered by an earlier one.

items.sixtySeconds: is and switch expressions. Match shape, bind a variable, compiler watches exhaustiveness.

items.question: When do you use a switch expression instead of if/else for auth providers?
items.answer: When the set of shapes is closed enough that missing a provider should be a compile-time or obvious runtime gap. Each arm returns a value. Learning Tools Interoperability (LTI) 1.3 versus an OpenID Connect (OIDC) bearer versus a legacy API key become property and list patterns, not nested ifs that forget a combination. Keep side effects out of arms; call named methods. The discard arm should throw with the unmatched value, not silently default to a privileged path.

items.sixtySeconds: Closed set, one value per arm, throw on unknown. Property patterns for LTI versus OIDC versus API key.

items.question: How does with relate to immutability?
items.answer: Records are reference types (or record structs) with value-based equality and a compiler-generated copy constructor. with allocates a copy and sets the listed properties. Concurrent attempt-submit code can snapshot a scoring policy record and pass the copy into a worker without a lock around field writes. with does not deep-copy nested mutable lists; those still need their own immutability story.
followUps: Does with work on ordinary classes?
What is init versus set on the copied properties?
items.sixtySeconds: with copies a record. Original unchanged. Nested mutable collections are still shared.

items.question: Name four pattern kinds and one production use each.
items.answer: Declaration and type: if (seq is IList<T> list) for O(1) count. Relational: score bands on an attempt. Property: auth provider records. List: ragged CSV import rows with [_, kind, .., amount]. Logical not: is not null. Positional: Deconstruct on a record in a switch arm.
followUps: What does .. mean in a list pattern?
Can you use patterns in an is expression outside switch?
items.sixtySeconds: Type, property, relational, list. CSV rows and auth records are the stories to tell.
